papers.title: Process window and mechanical interlocking in friction stir welding of laser-textured Al-7075 and PEEK
papers.abstract: Polymer–metal hybrid joints are attractive for lightweight structural applications. However, their practical implementation is often limited by failure at the metal–polymer interface rather than by intrinsic material capability. To address this challenge, this work combines nanosecond laser-surface texturing with pinless Friction Stir Welding (FSW) to establish a controlled interfacial architecture in Al-7075/PEEK lap joints and systematically identify a stable, reproducible FSW processing window for reliable joint formation. Wave-shaped microgrooves are created on the aluminum surface by laser before joining to promote polymer-metal mechanical interlocking. Rotational speed, dwell time, and plunge displacement are varied, while joint integrity, groove preservation, and process stability are used as the evaluation criteria. A stable processing region was established primarily at 3000–4500 rpm, with dwell times of 2–6 s and plunge displacements of 0.1–0.2 mm, where sufficient polymer flow occurred without excessive thermal softening of PEEK or distortion of the microgrooves. Successful joints were obtained under restricted conditions at 6000 rpm, limited to low plunge displacement and short dwell time. Outside this processing window, higher rotational speed and longer dwell time were associated with PEEK over-softening and interfacial degradation, consistent with increased thermal input. In contrast, larger plunge displacement increases applied forging pressure and causes groove deformation, reducing interlocking efficiency. Statistical and post-failure analyses show that joint performance is governed primarily by mechanically driven interlocking arising from the interaction between the laser-defined microgrooves and the FSW parameters. The results provide a process-oriented framework for selecting FSW conditions that enable stable and repeatable fabrication of laser-textured polymer–metal load-bearing hybrid joints.

papers.title: Quantification of early-stage sigma phase nucleation in thermally aged 2205 duplex stainless steel at 850 °C: An integrated experimental, kinetic, and thermodynamic modelling approach
papers.abstract: Duplex stainless steels combine high strength and corrosion resistance, but exposure at 600-950 °C can precipitate brittle sigma (σ) and chi (χ) phases. This study examines early-stage intermetallic-phase evolution in 2205 duplex stainless steel aged at 850 °C using automated SEM image analysis, Avrami kinetics, Thermo-Calc equilibrium calculations and TC-PRISMA modelling. Bright-particle microstructural parameters were quantified across ageing times of 0.1-17 h. A two-stage transformation was identified: rapid nucleation within the first hour (area fraction rising from 0 to over 10%) followed by coarsening, with particle density peaking early then declining. Avrami analysis yielded n = 1.45 and k = 0.704, consistent with site-saturated nucleation at α/γ interfaces followed by diffusion-limited growth. Equilibrium calculations revealed that σ stability at 850 °C is highly sensitive to composition within the 2205 specification, particularly the minor elements silicon and copper. Two specification-compliant compositions lay on opposite sides of the σ solvus: reducing silicon and restoring copper, with no change to the major elements, raised the equilibrium σ fraction from zero to ∼20 vol.%. This implies that two compositions certified to the same 2205 grade can differ markedly in their susceptibility to sigma embrittlement at service temperature, a distinction not captured by the grade specification alone. For the measured composition, equilibrium predicts ∼23.5 vol.% sigma, comparable to the ∼19% measured after 17 h. TC-PRISMA simulations reproduced the early kinetics but required austenite as the matrix and under-predicted the long-time fraction, illustrating the limits of mean-field modelling for the ferrite-driven σ transformation.

papers.title: High-performance direct diffusion-bonded SiCp/Al composites joints via pulsed current: Strategy and mechanism for overcoming interfacial barriers
papers.abstract: : Precision-bonding of the SiCp/Al structure plays a decisive role in HPIM production. However, the oxide film and ∼5-fold melting temperature difference of SiC and Al matrix hinder the bonding process at a temperature below the melting point of Al alloy. This study aimed to overcome the above challenges, realize high-strength precision bonding of SiCp/Al under fully solid-state conditions, and thus support the iterative upgrading of HPIM. Herein, a practical strategy was proposed for the precision fabrication of SiCp/Al integrated structure: Pulsed current assisted diffusion bonding (PCDB) without filler materials. Elemental diffusion and deoxygenation reaction were synergistically stimulated at the interface domain by the interface-concentrated Joule heating. Therefore, a directly tight bond of Al/SiC sub-interface was formed at such a low temperature below the melting point of Al alloy. Simultaneously, the electroplastic effect enhanced dislocation motion within the Al matrix, thereby reducing the deformation resistance. Rapid closure of the bonding interface was thus achieved. Ultimately, PCDB yielded a direct bonding joint with a shear strength of 85.04 MPa and a deformation rate of merely 0.62% at 500 °C / 60 min / 10 MPa. Finally, the high-strength and micro-deformation bonding of SiCp/Al has been achieved, as a breakthrough that advances HPIM fabrication technology.

papers.title: Effect of Rolling Microstructure Uniformity on the Mechanical Properties of 34SiMnMo Ultra-High Strength Steel
papers.abstract: : The uniformity of rolling microstructure significantly affects the final microstructure and mechanical properties of the ultra-high strength steels. This work studies the influence of initial rolling microstructure uniformity on austenitization temperature, prior austenite grain size, tempered martensite microstructure, and tensile properties of 34SiMnMo steel. Uniform rolling introduces high density deformation substructures, improves deformation energy storage, and reduces austenitization temperature, which generates fine-grain heredity effect with prior austenite grains refined to 3.41 μm and forms a uniformly fine tempered martensite structure, achieving an ultimate tensile strength of 1956 MPa and a total elongation of 14.23%. In contrast, non-uniform rolled steel has a "fine grain—coarse grain—fine grain" layered structure along the thickness direction. Stress concentration occurs at the coarse/fine grain interface during the tensile process due to deformation incompatibility, which induces crack initiation and propagation along grain boundaries, limiting the enhancement of strong plasticity. This work provides theoretical data reference for the optimization of preparation process and engineering application of ultra-high strength steels.

papers.title: Modification of Fe-rich phases in Al-1Fe alloy by Al-5Ti-B grain refiner
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Fe is a typical impurity element in recycled aluminum alloys and tends to form coarse Fe-rich phases during solidification, thereby deteriorating ductility, toughness, and service reliability. To investigate how the Al-5Ti-B grain refiner affects the nucleation and growth behavior of Fe-rich phases, an Al-1Fe alloy was used as the model alloy. Al-5Ti-B, Al-10Ti, and Al-3B master alloys, as well as TiB 2 powder, were separately introduced. The phase constitution, morphological evolution, and interfacial crystallographic characteristics of Fe-rich phases were investigated using XRD, SEM, TEM, thermodynamic calculations, and DSC. The results show that 0.2 wt.% Al-5Ti-B changed eutectic Al 3 Fe from a long needle-like morphology to particle-like and short rod-like morphologies, reducing its average length from 10.74 μm to 1.64 μm, while its phase constitution and crystal structure remained essentially unchanged. In contrast, individual additions of Al-10Ti, Al-3B, or TiB 2 powder, and the combined addition of Al-10Ti and TiB 2 powder, did not produce a comparable modification effect. Further analysis indicates that bare TiB 2 particles exhibit a large lattice mismatch with Al 3 Fe and are unlikely to act as effective heterogeneous nucleation substrates. In contrast, TiB 2 particles in Al-5Ti-B with surface-associated Al 3 Ti two-dimensional compounds (2DC) may provide more favorable conditions for the heterogeneous nucleation of eutectic Al 3 Fe, while the refinement of α-Al dendrites may further suppress the growth of Al 3 Fe; the refinement of eutectic Al 3 Fe may result from the combined effects of these two mechanisms.
